name: catalyst
description: Typed TypeScript API clients from OpenAPI specs, with an MCP server for agents

showcase.tagline: Typed API clients from your OpenAPI specs, and an MCP server so your agent reads the API instead of guessing it.

highlights.title: One config, every client
highlights.text: `catalyst.config.json` lists your specs. `catalyst gen openapi` writes a typed TypeScript client for each, and `--check` fails CI when one drifts.

highlights.title: Answers from the spec
highlights.text: `catalyst api show` prints how to call an endpoint: the signature, the parameters, the response and its types. Nobody reads the raw JSON.

highlights.title: One small binary
highlights.text: A Native AOT build for Windows, with no .NET runtime to install. Toolkit puts it on your PATH and wires it into your agents.

mcpTools.name: list_clients

mcpTools.name: list_operations
mcpTools.text: Every endpoint as the generated client exposes it, filtered by words, tag or method.

mcpTools.name: show_operation
mcpTools.text: How to call one endpoint: the exact signature, a parameter table, the response and its types.

mcpTools.name: show_type
mcpTools.text: The TypeScript declaration of one generated type, with the types it references.

mcpTools.name: diff_spec
mcpTools.text: Breaking and non-breaking changes between two versions of a spec, in terms of the generated client.

mcpTools.name: generate_clients
mcpTools.text: Writes the clients to their output files, or checks them without writing anything.

steps.text: Add a page that shows one pet by its id. Use the Petstore client.
`client.get.pet(petId)` returns an `ApiResult<Pet>`. I'll call it from the page, show the name, and show the tag only when the API sends one. First, a check that the client is current.
The client matches the spec, so the page is built against the API as it is today.
